title: Detour
tagline: Race to 700 miles. Block. Repair. Counter.
teaser: A card road race: lay down miles to reach exactly 700 before your rival, throw flat tyres and red lights in their way, and save your immunities for the perfect counter. Watch every mile happen on the road, from coastal highways to night-time cities.

manPage.synopsis: detour — race to exactly 700 miles: lay distance, stop your rival with hazards, fix your own trouble, parry with a coup fourré.
manPage.description: Ken Arnold wrote mille for Berkeley Unix in 1982: a two-handed road-race card game against a computer that, as its source says in capitals, never discards a safety. Detour plays its rules and scoring exactly, ports that computer move for move as Classic, adds Rookie and Sly, a team game, and puts the race on a road you can watch, from the coast to the city.

howToPlay: Draw, then lay a card: miles to move (after a green light), a hazard to stop your rival, or a remedy for your own.
Exactly 700 ends the hand. Safeties guard you for the hand; lay one as its hazard hits for a coup fourré.
Keys: 1–6 or P pick a card, U uses it, D throws it away, C parries. Scores add up over hands to 5000.
